answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a decision, then slash that stake when later audits prove coordinated duplicate accounts violated the rules. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real value for every persona, rather than minting identities for free; splitting one stake across accounts does not meet the per-identity threshold. The system can use an ember of reputation, basalt-hard audit evidence, and echo patterns of synchronized behavior to trigger review, while preserving appeals for innocent agents.
